extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2025 program committee members (reviewers, area chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for reviewers of ICML 2025 submissions (main track and position paper track), including ethical rules, review-form items, process and timelines, and supplementary guidance for application-driven ML papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your areas of research expertise and “bid” on submissions; check reviewing assignments and notify the overseeing area chair of any problems (e.g., conflicts of interest); carefully review the correctness and merits of the submissions assigned; read and acknowledge the Authors’ Responses; actively participate in discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a high‑level duty list — be available for key reviewing periods and deadlines, follow the review form items, and participate in discussions and rebuttal acknowledgement as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare conflicts and notify ACs of assignment problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Check your reviewing assignments and notify the overseeing area chair of any problems (e.g., conflicts of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept assignments with conflicts; contact the area chair early if any problem arises so assignments can be adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding on submissions / indicate expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your areas of research expertise, and “bid” on submissions to review during the bidding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids (on abstracts) are used to help assign submissions. Participate in the bidding window (dates provided) to improve match quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and acknowledge authors' responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and acknowledge Authors’ Responses. Reviewers are required to explicitly acknowledge authors' rebuttals and agree to update the review if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement must be completed by the stated deadline; reviewers should click the 'Rebuttal Acknowledgement' button and may post additional comments/questions (5000 character limit). Failure to acknowledge is not compliant with process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active participation in discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively participate in discussions with other reviewers and ACs during discussion periods (AC-reviewer discussion period and author-reviewer discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post and respond to notes on OpenReview; discussions can resolve contradictions between reviews. Discussions with reviewers/ACs are not visible to authors; update reviews after discussions so authors get benefit of clarified evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow ICML code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the ICML code of conduct and affirm continued compliance while performing reviewer duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewing and participating in discussions, be polite, respectful, and professional. Unprofessional behavior can harm authors and the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: use of privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of privileged information (e.g., information and discussions about submissions) for any purpose other than reviewing is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use knowledge gained in the review process for outside advantage; report suspected misuse via ethics reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: collusion
rubrics_metrics.description: All forms of collusion, whether explicit or tacit (e.g., an arrangement between authors and reviewers, ACs, or SACs to obtain favorable reviews), are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected collusion via the Ethics Violation Reporting form; ICML oversight will investigate and may sanction parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: use of Generative AI tools for reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Generative AI tools (such as LLMs) for reviewing is strictly prohibited. Reviewers cannot use Generative AI tools to write their reviews, and reviewers cannot input any content from any submission or review into a Generative AI tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a firm ban — do not paste text from submissions or reviews into LLMs, nor generate review text with them. See ICML ethics guidelines for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (Main Track review-form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper (including the main findings, main results, main algorithmic/conceptual ideas, etc. that the paper claims to contribute). This summary should not be used to critique the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well‑written summary should not be disputed by the authors or other readers; use it to show you understood the submission, not to advance criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and Evidence (Main Track review-form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims made in the submission supported by clear and convincing evidence? If not, which claims are problematic and why? Do proposed methods and/or evaluation criteria make sense? Did you check proofs or experimental designs/analyses? Did you review supplementary material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about which claims you checked, which proofs or experiments you verified, and which supplementary materials you examined. Discuss issues and their severity; focus on substantiating major vs minor problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to Prior Works (Main Track review-form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: How are the key contributions related to broader scientific literature? Are there related works essential to understanding the paper that are not cited/discussed? How well‑versed are you with the literature related to this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete citations and comparisons (e.g., cite specific prior algorithms or results). Note your familiarity level (this answer is not visible to authors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Aspects (Main Track review-form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on other strengths and weaknesses such as originality, significance, and clarity. Be open‑minded about what counts as originality (e.g., novel combinations, removing assumptions, applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantiate any claimed strengths/weaknesses. Give actionable suggestions (including typos) and measure clarity relative to the intended ML audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions for Authors (Main Track review-form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate important questions for authors where the response would likely change your evaluation, clarify confusion, or address critical limitations. Number the questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve for impactful clarifications; explain how answers would change your evaluation. Keep questions focused so authors can respond within the rebuttal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Issues flagging and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe there are ethical issues with the paper, flag the paper for an ethics review and explain concerns in detail. Indicate which ethics expertise areas (e.g., discrimination, privacy, legal compliance, research integrity) would be useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided categories to guide triage. If flagged, give detailed reasons to help ethics reviewers assess the concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Recommendation (Main Track numeric scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate an overall recommendation on a 5-point scale: 5 Strong accept, 4 Accept, 3 Weak accept, 2 Weak reject, 1 Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh claims, evidence, significance, originality, and clarity. Ensure recommendation aligns with review text and substantiated issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position stated (Position Paper: Position)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper clearly state a position on a machine learning topic (policy, implementation, deployment, monitoring, etc.)? If it describes new research without advocacy, select No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position papers must state a position (argument, call to action, policy proposal, etc.) — evaluate whether the position is explicit and central to the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position in Title (Position Paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper’s title state the position? Can a reader understand the paper’s position from the title alone?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the title communicates the stance (Yes/No). Provide examples of titles that do or do not meet this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Summary (Position Paper review-form item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper, its contributions, and the position it advocates. This summary should not be used to critique the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with main track, provide a neutral, undisputed summary showing comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and Weaknesses (Position Paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a thorough assessment of strengths and weaknesses focusing on the stated position: Is it well supported with reasoning/evidence? Is the topic relevant to ICML? Is it likely to inspire discussion? Is it clearly argued and properly cited?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not comment on whether you agree with the position. Offer suggestions for improvement and note if the paper lacks a position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Support rating (1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a numerical rating (4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor) indicating how well the paper supports its position with clear reasoning and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this scale to quantify the strength of argumentation and evidence supporting the stated position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Significance rating (1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a numerical rating indicating how well the paper demonstrates the position is important in terms of scope, impact, timeliness, risks, benefits, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both community‑level importance and broader impacts when rating significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Discussion Potential rating (1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the paper’s potential to inspire constructive, useful discussion within the ICML community (4 excellent → 1 poor). Reviewer need not agree with the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess likelihood of generating productive community engagement and debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Argument Clarity rating (1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate clarity of presentation (writing style) using the 4-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider organization, lucidity, and accessibility to ICML readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Related Work rating (1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate degree to which the paper includes discussion of and citations to literature and events relevant to the stated position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness and relevance of the contextualization; missing essential citations should be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Questions and Ethics flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate important questions for authors (numbered), and flag ethical issues for ethics review if appropriate (with area selection and detailed concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions should target items that could change your assessment; ethical flags should be specific to help triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper: Overall Rating and Confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose overall recommendation on the 1–5 scale (same as main track) and indicate reviewer confidence on a 1–5 scale describing familiarity and care in the assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence conveys how much weight to place on the review given reviewer expertise and checking of details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of reviews and anonymity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews and discussion for all accepted papers will be made public on OpenReview after the reviewing period; authors of rejected papers may opt‑in. The identities of reviewers will be hidden from each other and visible only to ACs, SACs, and program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that content may become public; write reviews professionally and avoid revealing identity in review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent works policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors cannot expect to discuss other papers made publicly available within four months of the submission deadline; such recent papers should be considered concurrent/simultaneous. Use good judgement about whether non-peer‑reviewed public papers should be discussed, following subfield best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, consult the Area Chair. Explicit example: the 4‑month cutoff is adopted from AISTATS/ICLR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing process: reading and verifying claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Read assigned submissions carefully, critically, and with empathy. Verify proofs, check whether hypotheses are actually tested by experiments, and check whether empirical claims follow from results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is often the most time‑consuming part of review. Determine severity of issues, focus on major issues, but also point out minor fixable problems. Explicitly state what you checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding period and assignment timeline compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in the bidding period (dates provided); assignments occur in the stated submission assignment period and reviewing must occur within the reviewing window; reviews must be submitted by the review deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the timeline; be available for key periods (bidding, reviewing, rebuttal acknowledgement, AC discussions). Missing deadlines undermines process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' response and rebuttal protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have a rebuttal window (5000 character limit per response). Reviewers must acknowledge rebuttals by the acknowledgement deadline and may post additional comments/questions (5000 char). Authors may reply to additional comments by a later deadline. Limits on back‑and‑forth are enforced via custom buttons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only post additional comments early enough for author final response; confidential AC comments exist for procedural issues and should not be used to submit extra rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments for ACs (do not use for late rebuttals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can post confidential comments for ACs separate from rebuttal; this is for procedural/logistical comments and will be ignored if used for extra rebuttals or late points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat this mechanism as a place for substantive rebuttal — it will be ignored for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Guidelines for Application‑Driven ML submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For application‑driven papers, consider whether methods fit the problem; expect non‑standard datasets that should be documented/validated; compare to prior work outside ML as well as baseline ML methods; recognize originality can be novel combinations, datasets, or new evaluation framings; clarity should not require domain‑expert knowledge; significance may include potential impact on applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be flexible in evaluation metrics and baselines; encourage use‑informed datasets when well documented; judge clarity relative to an ML audience and value simple, applicable ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer professionalism and constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should create value for the authors and community by giving actionable feedback. Be polite, respectful, and professional. Substantiate comments about strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive suggestions, prioritize major issues, and avoid unprofessional language that could harm junior researchers. Use examples and concrete fixes where possible.
